title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Coupling DFT or multireference calculations, and machine-learning loops, with experiment is presented as a shift from empirical rare-earth design to theory-guided prediction of reactivity, magnetic coupling, electrochemistry, and high oxidation states.
explanation: DFT is used to support bimetallic electron transfer in a neutral Lu(II) CpIII complex and to quantify coupling through a tetraphenylbenzene tetraanion. Rare-earth doping of MOF-5 is mapped from HOMO–LUMO gap, dipole, adsorption energy, and charge distribution onto electrochemical performance. DFT plus CASSCF/NEVPT2 yields an ionisation-quotient criterion for which elements can reach high oxidation states. An automated platform and ML classify 780 condition sets for a nested Gd52Ni36 cluster and iterate toward better synthesis conditions.
scope: Computational and data-driven design of rare-earth molecules, clusters, and doped MOF electrodes.
conditions: DFT; CASSCF/NEVPT2 for the ionisation quotient; iterative experiment–learning over 780 condition sets for the nested cluster.
caveats: The outlook later notes that theoretical predictions still disagree with experiment, so these criteria are not treated as fully mature.
